questions.q: What gap did Databricks & Delta Lake's Structured Streaming material leave open?
options: It didn't cover purpose-built streaming tools like a time-series-optimized query language, sub-second alerting, or a high-volume event storage engine
It never covered streaming at all
It only worked with batch data, never streaming data
It required Unity Catalog to function
questions.explain: Structured Streaming was genuinely real streaming, but built on Spark's general-purpose DataFrame engine.

A synonym for Structured Streaming
A feature only available within a Lakehouse item

questions.q: What are the three new item types this chapter introduces?
options: Eventstream, Eventhouse/KQL Database, and Activator
Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Dataflow
Notebook, Pipeline, and Semantic Model
Capacity, Workspace, and OneLake
questions.explain: None of these existed in the Databricks & Delta Lake material — this is genuinely new territory.

questions.q: Why does "real-time" mean something more specific here than in Structured Streaming?
options: Real-Time Intelligence targets sub-second latency, while Structured Streaming's micro-batches process data seconds apart at best
There's no real difference between the two
Structured Streaming is actually faster than Real-Time Intelligence
Real-time only refers to batch jobs scheduled every hour
questions.explain: Lessons 29-34 on windowing and watermarks will make the technical reason for this difference concrete.

questions.q: What does Activator provide that a scheduled job doesn't?
options: Sub-second alerting directly on streaming data, with no scheduled job required
A way to schedule notebook runs every hour
A replacement for Eventhouse's storage
Access control for KQL databases
questions.explain: This is covered properly in Lesson 37, but previewed here as one of the three genuinely new pieces.
